title: Reading Comprehension Demo
note: One three-paragraph passage shared by three questions, plus a two-paragraph Critical Reasoning argument. On wide screens long passages sit beside the question, as on the real exam.

coral.title: Passage
text: For most of the twentieth century, marine biologists treated coral bleaching as a straightforward symptom of stress: when water temperatures rose, corals expelled the symbiotic algae that supply most of their energy, turned white, and, if conditions did not improve, starved. Under this view, a reef's survival depended almost entirely on how long a heat wave lasted.

Research over the past two decades has complicated that picture. Some colonies that bleach **recover within weeks**, while neighboring colonies of the same species, exposed to identical temperatures, die. One explanation is that corals can host several strains of algae, and certain strains tolerate heat far better than others. A coral that shifts toward a heat-tolerant strain after bleaching may survive the next warm season with little damage — a process some researchers call *symbiont shuffling*.

The finding has encouraged proposals to seed threatened reefs with heat-tolerant algae. Critics caution, however, that the tolerant strains often supply their hosts with less energy, so corals that rely on them may grow more slowly and reproduce less. A reef that survives by this route, they argue, may persist in a diminished form rather than truly recover.

questions.stem: The primary purpose of the passage is to
choices: argue that coral bleaching is less harmful than biologists once believed
describe a refinement of an earlier understanding of coral bleaching and note a reservation about a proposal it inspired
compare two competing explanations for why corals expel their symbiotic algae
advocate seeding threatened reefs with heat-tolerant strains of algae
explain why rising water temperatures cause corals to starve
questions.why:
Paragraph 1 gives the older view, paragraph 2 refines it (symbiont shuffling), and paragraph 3 reports a proposal and the critics' reservation.

(A) overstates the passage's claim, and (D) takes a side the author never takes.

questions.stem: According to the passage, the critics mentioned in the third paragraph are concerned that corals relying on heat-tolerant algae may
choices: bleach more frequently than other corals
be unable to shift back to their original algae
receive less energy and therefore grow and reproduce less
spread heat-tolerant algae to neighboring reefs
die within weeks of a heat wave
questions.why: The third paragraph says tolerant strains "often supply their hosts with less energy," so such corals "may grow more slowly and reproduce less."

questions.stem:
The passage suggests which of the following about two colonies of the same species exposed to identical temperatures, one of which survives bleaching and one of which dies?

Select the best answer.
choices: The surviving colony was exposed to the heat for a shorter period.
The surviving colony may have hosted, or shifted toward, a more heat-tolerant strain of algae.
The colony that died had already expelled all of its algae before the heat wave.
The surviving colony will grow faster than the colony that died would have.
Temperature plays no role in whether a colony survives bleaching.
questions.why: The passage offers symbiont shuffling as "one explanation" for why identically exposed colonies differ. (A) contradicts "identical temperatures"; (D) runs against the critics' point about slower growth.

stimulus.text:
Last year the town of Millbrook replaced its streetlights with brighter LED fixtures. In the twelve months since, reported car break-ins in the town center have fallen by 30 percent.

The town council concludes that the brighter lighting deterred would-be thieves and plans to install the same fixtures in the town's residential neighborhoods.

questions.stem: Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the council's conclusion?
choices: The LED fixtures use less electricity than the fixtures they replaced.
Residents of the neighborhoods have asked for brighter lighting.
During the same twelve months, the town began stationing a police patrol in the town center each night.
Car break-ins in neighboring towns were roughly unchanged over the same period.
Some residents find the new lighting too harsh.
questions.why:
A new nightly patrol is an alternative cause for the drop, so the lighting may not be responsible.

(D) actually strengthens the conclusion by ruling out a region-wide trend.

title: Data Insights Warm-Up (demo)
note: Four questions in 10 minutes. Included mainly to show that the engine handles passages, tables, multi-select, and two-part analysis, not just Problem Solving.

stimulus.text: Quarterly results for four regional offices of a logistics firm (revenue in $ millions):

questions.stem: Select every statement that the table supports.
choices: East had the largest percent increase in revenue from Q1 to Q2.
The office with the highest Q2 revenue also had the highest Q2 margin.
Total Q2 revenue for the four offices exceeded total Q1 revenue.
South was the only office whose revenue declined from Q1 to Q2.
questions.why: East grew 50% versus North's 25%, so the first statement holds. West had the highest Q2 revenue but the lowest margin, so the second fails. Totals were 66.0 in Q1 and 72.5 in Q2, and only South declined.

questions.stem: A caterer buys x trays of sandwiches at $40 each and y trays of salad at $25 each. She buys 12 trays in total and spends $405. Select the number of sandwich trays and the number of salad trays.
questions.why: 40x + 25(12 − x) = 405 → 15x = 105 → x = 7 sandwich trays and 5 salad trays.

stimulus.text: City officials note that since a bike-share program launched downtown two years ago, downtown car traffic has fallen 9%. They conclude that the bike-share program caused the decline in car traffic.

questions.stem: Which of the following, if true, most weakens the officials' conclusion?
choices: Bike-share memberships grew steadily over the two-year period.
Two large downtown employers shifted most of their staff to remote work during the same period.
A neighboring city with no bike-share program saw car traffic rise by 2%.
Most bike-share trips downtown are shorter than one mile.
The city spent less on the bike-share program than it had budgeted.
questions.why: An alternative cause for the traffic decline undermines the causal claim. The remote-work shift explains fewer cars without the bike-share program doing the work.

stimulus.text: A survey of 400 commuters found that 180 drive, 120 take transit, 60 bike, and the remainder walk.

questions.stem: What percent of the surveyed commuters walk?
